statements.text: From a cybersecurity provision that will help manufacturers in the Inland Empire, to Deepfake and anti-corruption measures to keep our country safe, to support for Minority-Serving Institutions that will ensure a diverse STEM workforce at the DoD, the vote today was a win for our community and our ideals.

statements.text: In the wake of SolarWinds, the Federal Government has prioritized harnessing the power of AI to create endpoint detect and response systems that can detect anomalous behavior on a network. Is there presently AI technology that could have prevented SolarWinds' intrusion or could have detected it earlier?
statements.context: US congressional hearing on emerging technologies and security risks, where a lawmaker questions an expert panel on AI's role in cyber defense.

statements.text: I have found the discourse about AI to be pessimistic to the point of apocalyptic. So, I am curious, what do you see not only as the greatest risk, but also the greatest reward of AI when it comes to consumer protection in the field of financial services?
statements.context: US congressional hearing on the Semi-Annual Report of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection.

statements.text: Artificial intelligence is a powerful, transformative tool that can improve the efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability of Congress. However, AI could also bring unintended consequences. It opens the door to issues about authenticity and quality of work. As this Committee looks at AI in the legislative branch, we must diligently look at AI innovation and its impacts on our society. Is AI going to be used to write bills, to solve some of mankind's greatest problems? How will we continue to center the human experience on legislation? Is AI going to be used to automate and expand the ability of special interests to influence Members of Congress or our staff?
statements.context: Opening remarks at a House Administration Committee hearing on AI innovations within the legislative branch.

statements.text: How can AI be improved to help staff monitor their casework load, right, to help improve communication, responses to our constituents? That is what I am looking for.
statements.context: Spoken during a House hearing on AI innovations within the legislative branch.

statements.text: How do we protect personal data that is very sensitive personal data that is shared with our offices if we utilize a system like AI to help process these casework?
statements.context: Question posed during a House hearing on AI innovations within the legislative branch.

A.I. provides a path to prosperity at home and abroad. I introduced the International Artificial Intelligence Research Partnership Act to ensure the U.S. leads the way in ensuring the next generation of technological systems will support our values. 
https://t.co/owEBR4kmdV

In order to lead and ensure AI remains a tool for good around the globe, the U.S. must foster and strengthen international collaboration and partnerships for the research, development, and eventual implementation of artificial intelligence, especially as AI technologies penetrate more deeply into daily life. I introduced the International Artificial Intelligence Research Partnership Act because the United States must never cede its global leadership when it comes to disruptive technologies.
statements.venue: Press release on introducing the International AI Research Partnership Act of 2024

statements.text: This legislation seeks to cultivate and expand the research and development of artificial intelligence to ensure new AI tools and real-world applications adhere to the shared values of the United States and its allies and in so doing contribute to security, uphold democratic principles, foster economic prosperity, and sustain the dignity of every human life.
statements.venue: Press release on introducing the International AI Research Partnership Act of 2024

statements.text:
The @calpolypomona AI Conference provided a great opportunity to explore AI's future and its impact on education, innovation, and the economy. 

As an advocate for responsible AI, I know cross-sector collaboration is key to ensuring technology benefits everyone.

It should be the highest strategic priority of the United States to pursue AI dominance with the fierce urgency of the Manhattan Project. In the 20th century, the U.S. and Nazi Germany were locked in a high-stakes race to develop the first atomic bomb. In the 21st century, the United States and China are competing in a new strategic arms race _ the race for artificial superintelligence _ and the first country to reach ASI will likely emerge as the superpower of the 21st century.
statements.context: Rep. Torres poses the question during a hearing or event titled "Algorithms and Authoritarians: Why U.S. AI Must Lead," addressing an expert witness about the strategic framing of the US-China AI competition.

statements.text: When it comes to energy, China is outbuilding the United States by a ratio of 8 to 1, and yet at a time when the AI revolution has put unprecedented strain on the U.S. energy grid, the present reconciliation bill, to be blunt, would all but repeal the tax credits for clean energy.
statements.context: Rep. Ritchie Torres questions a witness at a hearing on U.S. AI leadership and energy policy.

statements.text: It is 90 percent, and solar is the most rapidly deployable, scalable energy source, and it just seems deeply self-destructive for the United States to restrict the number of electrons available to the AI revolution. I have a question about the export controls. I know you are supportive of it, Mr. Clark. Do you think the export controls were properly designed when put in place back in 2022 because I have heard concerns that even though the chips to which China had access had less computational power, it actually had more memory bandwidth than the best GPUs. So was that a fatal flaw in the original export controls?
statements.context: Rep. Ritchie Torres questions a witness at a hearing or event titled 'Algorithms and Authoritarians: Why U.S. AI Must Lead.'

statements.text: Can AI—I guess I was going to ask, can AI be harnessed to expand access to capital, to expand access to credit? One of my frustrations—I have real frustrations with traditional credit scoring methodology. Can AI detect new patterns of evaluating creditworthiness?
statements.context: Remarks delivered during a hearing on AI in the U.S. financial system.

statements.text: Because I know Members of Congress are irreplaceable, but I am wondering if bankers and traders are replaceable by AI. [...] What is the impact of AI on concrete applications like credit scoring, loan approvals, fraud prevention and detection? Like, does AI lead to more loan approvals or fewer? Does it lead to more inclusive credit scoring or less inclusive credit scoring? What is the outcome so far.
statements.context: Remarks delivered during a congressional hearing on AI in the U.S. financial system.

statements.text: AI is the most transformative technology of our time. The rise of generative AI could prove to be as revolutionary as the advent of writing or the advent of the printing press. Whether AI will create a better world or a worse world, no one knows for sure.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Rep. Torres at a congressional hearing on AI in the U.S. financial system.

statements.text: Private credit, banking, insurance, and AI CapEx are becoming increasingly interconnected. The AI sector is experiencing the largest capital boom since the railroads of the late 19th century, and AI CapEx has become a disproportionate driver of both economic growth and equity market performance. To what extent do you view the entanglement of private credit, banking, insurance, and multi-trillion-dollar AI CapEx as a potential source of systemic risk?
statements.context: House Oversight Subcommittee hearing on prudential regulators, where a member questions the Federal Reserve and others about AI-driven financial-system risk.

statements.text: If the United States is going to remain a global leader in innovation, we must adopt clear and harmonized rules that support technological progress while also protecting consumers and preserving market integrity.
statements.context: Rep. Torres delivers remarks and questions witnesses at a Financial Services Committee hearing on AI innovation in financial services.

statements.text: You see, I am pro-AI. My whole life is integrated with ChatGPT and Gemini. So, for me, the question is not whether we should have AI. [...] The question is, who should pay for it, right? Should the cost be borne by working-class families and small businesses, or should it be borne by the owners and operators of the data centers?
statements.context: Remarks at a financial-services AI innovation event, discussing the cost burden of AI infrastructure.

statements.text: Does anyone here have any thoughts on how we can harness the power of AI to build an underwriting system that is more predictive, more inclusive, and more representative of the full financial reality of working-class Americans?
statements.context: Rep. Torres poses a question to panelists at a financial-services AI policy event.

statements.text: Relying too heavily on AI-generated bill text could introduce errors, create unintended legal consequences, or result in language that does not accurately reflect a member's policy intent. [...] That responsibility cannot be outsourced to a chatbot.
